lines: Once upon a time, in the city of Shiraz, Iran, there was a famous poet named Sheikh Saadi.
Like many other poets and philosophers, he lived a very simple life.
One day, a rich man invited him, along with many rich and important people from the city, to a big wedding for his daughter.
The poet accepted the invitation and decided to go.
On the wedding day, the rich man who was hosting the wedding stood at the gate to welcome the guests.
Many rich people from the city came in their best clothes.
The poet wore simple clothes that were not special or expensive.
Even though he waited for someone to talk to him, no one looked at him.
Even the host didn’t greet him and looked away.
The poet quietly left the party and went to a nearby shop.
There, he rented a fancy coat decorated with gold.
It made him look like a new person.
He returned to the party.
This time, the host welcomed him warmly.
He even hugged him, as he would do to an old friend, and praised his fancy clothes.
The poet didn’t say a word, and the host led him to the dining room.
The host gave him a nice seat and brought him a bowl of chicken soup.
Suddenly, the poet dipped the corner of his coat into the soup as if he were feeding it.
Everyone looked at him in surprise.
The host asked, “Sir, what are you doing?”
The poet replied calmly, “When I wore simple clothes, no one noticed me.
But now you are kind because of my coat.
So this party is for my clothes, not for me.”
